newsitem.title: UK: BA to start talks with cabin crew on Weds.
newsitem.headline: BA to start talks with cabin crew on Weds.

text.p: British Airways said on Monday it planned to start talks with BASSA, its main cabin crew union, on how to make the 42 million pounds ($70.5 million) in savings required by BA management in a pay dispute.
"Talks with the cabin crew will be held at 1000 BST (0900 GMT) on Wednesday at London Heathrow airport," a BA spokesman said in a telephone interview.
The spokesman said the cabin crew talks would be conducted through the conciliation service ACAS.
No union representative was immediately available to comment.

BASSA, a division of the Transport and General Workers' Union (T&G) has accepted in principle the need for the target 42 million pound savings, part of the airline's 1.0 billion pound cost-cutting drive.
But union leaders say they want BA to consider their own alternative proposals on how to make the savings.

BA said earlier on Monday that as long as the proposals met its target figure in a way acceptable to all parties, it would then seek a process to move things forward jointly with BASSA and Cabin Crew 89, the second cabin crew union.

The dispute over the pay restructuring programme led to a 72-hour strike by cabin crew earlier in the month, an action that disrupted hundreds of flights and, BA estimates, cost the company tens of millions of pounds. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
